ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the straight line $y=kx+b$ ($k\neq 0$) passes through points $(2,0)$ and $(0,-3)$. What is the range of values of $x$ when $y>0$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the equation of the line be $y=kx+b$. This line intersects the x-axis at the point $(2,0)$, and it passes through the first, third, and fourth quadrants. From the graph, it is evident that\\
when $x>2$, the value of $y$ is greater than $0$,\\
therefore, the range of $x$ is $\boxed{x>2}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, the straight line $y=kx+b$ ($k\neq 0$) passes through points $(2,0)$ and $(0,-3)$. What is the range of values of $x$ when $y>0$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a straight line slanting upward to the right, passing through the point (2,0) marked on the x-axis, and passing through the point (0,-3) marked on the y-axis. Reasoning: The straight line is y=kx+b, passing through (0,-3), so b=-3. Passing through (2,0) and (0,-3), the slope k=(0-(-3))/(2-0)=3/2. Therefore the equation of the straight line is y=(3/2)x-3. Require y>0, that is (3/2)x-3>0, solving gives x>2.
